title: Three Summers and One Short Shadow
subtitle: 动物世界 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 动物世界（人与自然·自然生态·动物世界）
meta: 主题语境：动物世界（人与自然·自然生态·动物世界）　|　核心词汇：fish　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 fish 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1967 my grandfather ① caught a fish that no angler in the lake would have measured, and he said the catching was the whole of the summer. The ② fish, meaning the creature itself and not the dish, ran three summers and stayed unmeasured in the book; a fish, he said, is the only thing in a lake that is judged by how long it is left unmeasured.

Every ③ fish in that lake had the same short shadow beside it, and the ④ fish at the far bank, meaning the one they kept for the children and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A fish, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to measure; my grandfather said the measuring is the part that fills three summers.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the fish was the whole of the matter, meaning the person and not the creature. The ⑥ fish, meaning the person and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody measures; fish, he said, is either something you catch or the only word that means both a creature and a person. He said the person is the part they remember.

By 1974 the ⑦ fish had become a line in a plan, and the plan had become an argument about the short shadow. The ⑧ fish of the whole thing, my grandfather wrote in July, was one lake and three summers of measuring; fish, he said, is either the one at the far bank or the reason you learned to measure. He said the measuring was never mentioned.

The ⑨ fish I remember is the one measured in the plan, which closed in 1976 and is still described as the quietest in the lake. A ⑩ fish, my mother said in 1978, is the only one that improves by being measured; every fish, she said, is a person that has agreed to look like a creature. She said the person was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 鱼（指湖里每一条旁边的那一条）
B. n. 鱼（指那一条本身，与盘中菜肴相对）
C. 固定搭配：catch a fish 捕到一条鱼
D. n. 鱼（指留给孩子们的那一条）

F. n. 鱼（指计划里写到、被量过的那一条）
G. n. 家伙；大人物（a big fish，指一件事里人人都等却无人量过的那样人）
H. n. 家伙（抽象总称，指人人都等却无人量过的那样人）

answers.why: catch a fish 意为“捕到一条鱼”，1967 年祖父捕到了一条湖上没有一位垂钓者肯量过的鱼。
fish 意为“鱼”，指那一条本身而不是盘中菜肴，它经过了三个夏天而在簿子上没有尺寸。
fish 意为“鱼”，指湖里每一条旁边的那一条，每一条旁边都有同一道短短的影子。
fish 意为“鱼”，指留给孩子们的那一条，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
fish 意为“家伙、大人物”，指一件事里人人都等却无人量过的那样人，叔叔说这个大人物就是那件事的全部。
fish 意为“家伙”，指人人都等却无人量过的那样人而不是那一条鱼，是事情里人人都等、却无人量过的人。
fish 意为“鱼”，指计划里写到、被量过的那一条，到 1974 年这一条成了计划里的一行。
fish 意为“鱼”，祖父七月写道，整件事的鱼之事是一个湖和三个夏天的量过。
fish 意为“鱼”，我记得的是计划里量过的那一条，1976 年结束了，至今仍被说成湖里最安静的一条。
fish 为抽象总称，母亲 1978 年说，一条鱼是唯一会因为被好好量过而变得更好的东西。
